issues.body: require_one_side_bound is only a public helper. This diff does not call it from wire::derive_grants or any other real admission-path boundary, so controller-authored .acr text can still reach evaluation without the advertised refusal. That conflicts with the research/README claims that the guard refuses unbounded rules and leaves the stated P8 safety obligation unenforced unless every caller remembers an optional pre-check.
issues.fix_hint: Invoke the guard at the single shared boundary before controller-authored rule text reaches derive_grants/evaluation, propagate denial fail-closed, and add an integration test proving an unseeded .acr rule is rejected by that real path (plus a seeded rule still succeeds). If this PR intentionally provides analysis only, remove claims that the operational path is guarded and explicitly leave enforcement as unresolved work.
issues.title: Fail-closed seeding guard is not enforced on the real .acr path

issues.body: is_var recognizes only '?' variables, so a rule-body blank-node label such as '_:x' is treated as a constant by term_bound. In N3 rule formulae blank nodes are existential/formula-scoped nodes, not a fixed externally bound endpoint. Consequently a body like `{ _:x p:linkedTo ?o } => { ?o p:ok p:v }` can pass the one-side-bound guard even though its subject does not provide a constant-side lookup, undermining the conservative fail-closed claim.
issues.fix_hint: Model blank-node labels according to N3 formula semantics and do not count them as constant seeds (or reject them as unsupported). Add a regression test through require_one_side_bound showing that a blank-node-labelled body endpoint cannot make an otherwise unbound atom pass.
issues.title: Blank-node labels are incorrectly accepted as bound constants

verdict.summary: The cost meter and its tests are internally consistent as a deterministic count of coarse gate operations, but the decidability guard is not connected to the controller-authored .acr execution path it is meant to protect. The change therefore does not complete the stated fail-closed safety obligation: existing callers can continue handing unseedable rules directly to derive_grants, while the documentation says the guard refuses them. The parser also treats blank-node labels in rule bodies as constants, although formula-scoped blank nodes are existential rather than fixed bound values, allowing an unsafe seed shape to be classified as one-side-bound.
